test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 06 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
**Given below are two statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Read and mark the correct options:

Assertion (A):**

The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, promotes e-filing and virtual trials to expedite the justice delivery system.

**Reason (R):**

The integration of technology aims to reduce case pendency and enhance accessibility to justice.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false, but R is true.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, is part of the reforms aimed at modernizing the criminal justice delivery system in India.
 
• The Sanhita promotes e-filing of cases and virtual trials to facilitate faster and more efficient legal proceedings.
 
• Virtual trials aim to reduce logistical challenges and expedite the resolution of pending cases in the courts.
 
• Technological integration under BNSS is designed to enhance accessibility to justice, especially for remote and marginalized communities.
 
• The focus is on leveraging technology to address case backlogs and improve overall transparency in the justice system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **E-filing:** Refers to the electronic submission of legal documents, enabling litigants and lawyers to file cases online without physical visits to the court.
 
• **Virtual Trials:** These are court proceedings conducted via video conferencing or other digital platforms, ensuring continuity of justice even during emergencies like pandemics.
 
• **Case Pendency:** India’s judicial system faces a significant backlog of cases, with millions of cases pending across various courts, making swift reforms necessary.
 
• **Accessibility to Justice:** Leveraging technology makes the justice system more inclusive, reducing barriers for people in rural areas or those with limited resources.
 
• **Judicial Reforms:** BNSS, 2023, is part of a series of legislative updates aimed at modernizing colonial-era laws, such as replacing the Indian Penal Code (IPC), Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), and Evidence Act.
